full_judgment:
2. The petitioners in both the Rules are pre-emptee. The proceeding of pre-emption is under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The opposite party filed pre-emption cases. He is a co-sharer and the pre-emptee does not deny that he is a stranger. The pre-emption Miscellaneous case Nos. 18 and 19 of 1992 were filed in time and making necessary deposits in time. The trial Court after hearing the pre-emption cases analogously allowed the pre-emption cases on contest by the judgment and order dated 11-8-92. 

 3. The pre-emptee took the Miscellaneous Appeals 200 and 201 of 1992 against the judgment and order of the pre-emption in Miscellaneous cases 19 of 1992 and 18 of 1992 respectively. The impugned judgments and orders in both the appeals are similar, dated 19-5-98, passed by the same Court of the Additional District Judge, Dhaka. When the appeals were proceeding and were being contested by the pre-emptor, the pre-emptee filed an applications for noting by the appellate Court that the original pre-emption Miscellaneous Cases had already abated for non-substitution of the heirs of the opposite parties 20 and 21, namely Monir Hossain and Awlad Hossain respectively after their death. The appellate Court by its impugned order dated 19-5-98 rejected the applications finding, inter alia, that since those opposite parties were non-contesting in the pre-emption cases substitution of their heirs is not necessary. Against that orders of the appellate Court the pre-emptee petitioners have obtained the present Rules. So the question poses before this Court to decide whether the pre-emption proceedings under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act abated for non-substituting of the heirs of those opposite parties 20 and 21 who were non-contesting. Admittedly those opposite parties did not file any written objection for contesting in the pre-emption cases. At the appellate stage, this objection was taken by the pre-emptee as to abatement of the pre-emption cases and it was urged before the appellate Court that, consequently and on the same ground the appeal also should he allowed because the original pre-emption cases had already abated, and thus the trial Court committed illegality in allowing the pre-emption. 

 "Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-rule (3), the plaintiff shall not be required to substitute and shall be exempt from the necessity of substituting the legal representative of any such defendants who has failed to file a written statement or who having filed, it, has failed to appear and contest the suit at the hearing; and judgment may in such a case be pronounced against the deceased defendant notwithstanding the death of such defendant and shall have the same force and effect as if it had been pronounced before the death took place." 

 Miah Abdul Gafur, the learned Counsel submits that in pre-emption proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which is a special law, the provisions of Order 22 rule 4(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure shall not apply, but he could not convince the Court, in that case, what provision of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act will be applicable and for what reason, the said provision of the Civil Procedure Code will not apply, Mr. Gafur hopelessly failed to show that there is any procedure for substitution which has been embodied within the section 96 or within the four corners of the State Acquisition and Tenancy 

 "Para 27, : In the case of Jamiyat Ali vs Mrs Chemon Ara Begum and others, 20 DLR 480, where it was correctly held that in a proceeding under section 96 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the provision of Order 1, rule 13, Code of Civil Procedure was applicable and that the objection as to the defect of party, which was not taken before the trial could not be taken during the trial or at the appellate stage." 

 9. Mr. Gafur also submits that since the provision of section 96(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has distinctly provided that all the co-sharers to be made parties in a pre-emption proceeding, in that view also the pre-emption cases, were not maintainable for non-substituting of the heirs of the said deceased opposite parties. The submission with the said analogy has no legal use or force in the present legal conflict. Here the question of substitution is to be decided and question of non-joinder of the heirs of the non-contesting deceased opposite parties does not arise. The intention of the law makers was that, when a pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act chance should be given to all co-sharers to pray for rateable pre-emption if so desired, as provided under section 96 (4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, which cannot he invoked for the present purpose.
